free_tier.stated: Free, keyless REST API for global solar and meteorological data (hourly, daily, monthly and climatology levels; daily series from 1981); no numeric request quota is published, the vendor says there is no set rate limit and usage is monitored.
free_tier.notes: A single point takes up to 20 parameters on the daily API and 15 on the hourly API; regional requests take one parameter. Bulk path: the complete datastore is in public S3 buckets (s3://nasa-power as Zarr, s3://power-datastore as NetCDF, us-west-2), read with no AWS account, which bypasses the API's rate, transfer and timeout limits. Recent meteorological values are replaced by climate-quality values within 2 to 3 months.

per_object_cap.stated: 20 parameters per single-point request on the daily API, 15 on the hourly API, 1 per regional request

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

egress.terms: JSON, CSV, NetCDF and ASCII answers; the S3 buckets are free of charge to everyone

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS GET at power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/{daily,hourly,monthly,climatology}/{point,regional}, with OpenAPI pages; Zarr and NetCDF files in anonymous S3 buckets
tooling: any HTTP client; any S3 client reads the buckets with no signing; Python tutorials for Zarr access are published by the project
chaining: A keyless solar and reanalysis-based weather source for coordinates worldwide; use the S3 Zarr store for bulk pulls instead of looping the API.

limits.value: unverified: no numeric limit is published; the vendor says there is no set rate limit and usage is limited to support equitable access

binding_note: No request rate is published, so the parameter cap per request is the number that shapes a large pull; the S3 buckets have no such cap.

identity_cost.detail: No sign-up and no key: keyless API calls and anonymous bucket listings answered HTTP 200; the AWS registry page says no AWS account is required.

reliability_note: Repeating the same location or flooding with synchronous requests can get an application blocked; overload answers HTTP 429.
confidence_note: A keyless daily point call and an anonymous bucket listing were made and kept; the rate limit is not published and was not driven.
